hardware: CPU only (no GPU used for this benchmark)
why_speedup_missed: sqlite-vec 0.1.9 is the latest release and its vec0 KNN is brute force, not ANN.
Measured directly: per-candidate-vector cost stays flat at ~1.6-1.9 us from 5k to 100k rows, which is linear in N. An ANN index would show sub-linear scaling.
The observed 1.55x is only what vec0's C loop gains over the pure-Python exact path.
Reaching a real 10x+ needs a different vector index (hnswlib / FAISS / USearch) or a sqlite-vec release that ships ANN.
keep_vec0_because: C-speed search rather than a Python loop
metadata + partition-key pruning, so constrained KNN scans less
recall@10 is exactly 1.000, i.e. it is a correct drop-in for exact
a clean seam for swapping a real ANN backend in later
reproduce: AI_DB_BENCH_N=100000 AI_DB_BENCH_DIM=1024 AI_DB_BENCH_QUERIES=50 pytest tests/test_bench_vectors.py -m bench -q -s
